title: Initiative Coordinator at forNature in Panama: Full-Time Opportunity to Support the United Nations Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature
summary: The global movement to recognize and protect the Rights of Nature continues to gain momentum, and forNature is seeking an experienced professional to play a central role in one of its most ambitious international initiatives. The organization is currently recruiting a full-time Initiative Coordinator based in Panama City, Panama , to support the operational, strategic, institutional, and diplomatic coordination of the initiative advancing the adoption of a United Nations Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature (UDRoN). This is a unique opportunity for professionals with experience in project coordination, international relations, environmental governance, multilateral diplomacy, and institutional engagement to contribute directly to an initiative with global environmental significance. The successful candidate will coordinate complex international workstreams involving governments, legal experts, communications professionals, civil society organizations, diplomatic missions, and international institutions while working closely with the Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Panama (MiAmbiente). About the Initiative The United Nations Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature (UDRoN) initiative seeks to advance international recognition of Nature as a subject of rights through the United Nations system. The Initiative Coordinator will play a critical role in ensuring that all aspects of the initiative progress efficiently by coordinating institutional relationships, facilitating communication among stakeholders, tracking deliverables, and supporting diplomatic and legal processes. The position sits at the intersection of environmental policy, international diplomacy, legal coordination, strategic communications, and institutional management. Position Overview The Initiative Coordinator will serve as the central coordination hub for the initiative. Working closely with forNature and MiAmbiente , the coordinator will oversee operational implementation while ensuring that all teams remain aligned with project priorities, timelines, and strategic objectives. The role combines project management, stakeholder coordination, diplomatic engagement, documentation, communications management, and international event coordination.Although the position is remote, the successful applicant must be based in Panama City and remain available for meetings with Panamanian institutions, as well as occasional international travel. Major Responsibilities The Initiative Coordinator will oversee numerous interconnected workstreams. 1. Coordinate the Entire Initiative Team The successful candidate will coordinate professionals across multiple disciplines, including: Attorneys Legal advisors Communications specialists Public Relations teams Campaign consultants Digital communications consultants Graphic designers Civil society engagement leads Business engagement leads Institutional advisors Responsibilities include: Acting as the central coordination point Organizing internal workflows Monitoring deadlines Tracking assignments Coordinating deliverables Ensuring smooth communication across all teams Monitoring approvals Supporting strategic decision-making Facilitating collaboration across departments 2. Lead Cross-Functional Team Coordination The coordinator will organize and facilitate: Internal meetings Strategic planning sessions Briefings Coordination meetings Follow-up discussions They will also prepare: Agendas Meeting summaries Action items Briefing notes Follow-up communications The role requires maintaining alignment across legal, diplomatic, operational, communications, campaign, and institutional workstreams. 3. Serve as the Main Institutional Liaison One of the most important aspects of this position involves serving as the day-to-day operational liaison between forNature and the Government of Panama. Responsibilities include: Coordinating with MiAmbiente Working with the Office of International Technical Cooperation Supporting coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Managing institutional documentation Tracking ministerial approvals Following document management procedures Maintaining continuity during government personnel transitions Escalating institutional bottlenecks when necessary 4. Support Multilateral Diplomacy The Initiative Coordinator will provide operational support for international diplomatic engagement. Responsibilities include: Preparing briefing materials Developing talking points Coordinating bilateral meetings Supporting Panama s Permanent Missions Assisting embassies Preparing diplomatic correspondence Monitoring United Nations calendars Tracking General Assembly timelines Monitoring multilateral environmental agreement processes The coordinator will also maintain records of: Member State engagement Government focal points Expressions of support Pending diplomatic actions 5. Document Production and Knowledge Management The coordinator will oversee document development and information management across the initiative. Key responsibilities include: Creating the initiative s Operations Manual Drafting institutional documents Producing concept notes Preparing FAQs Writing meeting records Maintaining terminology consistency Managing bilingual documentation Tracking document versions Protecting confidential materials Organizing centralized documentation systems Documentation will be prepared in both English and Spanish . 6. Support the For Nature Coalition of States The coordinator will help expand and manage the growing Coalition of States supporting the initiative. Responsibilities include: Maintaining communication with participating countries Tracking engagement records Supporting onboarding processes Preparing participation documents Coordinating announcements Managing membership materials Supporting signing ceremonies during international events 7. Build Relationships with Key Stakeholders The Initiative Coordinator will engage a broad range of stakeholders including: Government institutions International organizations United Nations agencies Academic institutions Research organizations Development partners Philanthropic organizations Business associations Private sector organizations Professional organizations Legal institutions Cultural institutions Subnational governments The coordinator will also support engagement with: Civil society organizations Indigenous Peoples Traditional authorities Community leaders Local communities 8. Coordinate International Events Responsibilities include organizing the initiative s participation in international meetings and conferences by managing: Side event proposals Concept notes Accreditation Speaker coordination Logistics Official programme registration 9. Promote an Intercultural and Politically Sensitive Approach The coordinator must ensure that implementation reflects: Respect for Indigenous worldviews Cultural diversity Territorial knowledge systems Diplomatic sensitivities Institutional priorities Political contexts surrounding the Rights of Nature movement Required Qualifications Applicants should possess substantial professional experience in areas such as: Project coordination Programme management Institutional coordination Campaign implementation Candidates should demonstrate the ability to: Coordinate multiple projects simultaneously Manage competing priorities Meet strict deadlines Work independently Communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders Handle confidential information professionally Essential Skills Successful applicants should have: Professional fluency in English Professional fluency in Spanish Excellent organizational skills Strong written communication skills Strong verbal communication skills Excellent stakeholder management abilities Experience preparing reports and institutional documents Experience managing calendars and workplans Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams Preferred Experience Additional advantages include experience with: Government institutions International organizations Civil society networks Environmental initiatives Multilateral diplomacy United Nations processes Environmental law Rights of Nature frameworks Diplomatic drafting Institutional relationship management Panamanian public administration Additional Requirements Applicants should also possess: A valid passport A valid United States visa Availability for international travel Ability to coordinate across multiple time zones Strong intercultural awareness Respect for Indigenous leadership and governance systems Work Location The position is based in: Panama City, Panama The work arrangement is: Full-time Remote Attendance at meetings with Panamanian institutions when required Participation in in-person national and international engagements as necessary The engagement is structured as an independent contractor relationship rather than direct employment. Compensation forNature offers: Competitive industry compensation Salary based on qualifications Salary based on years of relevant experience Application Requirements Interested applicants should submit: A current CV or résumé A brief cover letter written in either English or Spanish Applications should be emailed via (info@fornature.org) with the subject line: Application – Initiative Coordinator Application Deadline Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled . There is no fixed application deadline , and candidates with immediate availability are strongly preferred . Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since recruitment may conclude once a suitable candidate has been identified. Equal Opportunity Employer forNature is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. The organization does not discriminate on the basis of: Race Color Religion Sex Gender identity Sexual orientation National origin Age Disability Any other legally protected status The organization strongly encourages applications from: Women Indigenous professionals Individuals from historically marginalized communities. learn more about the opportunity HERE Why You Should Apply This position offers an exceptional opportunity to contribute to an internationally significant environmental initiative that seeks to shape the future of global environmental governance. Professionals interested in diplomacy, international law, environmental protection, public policy, institutional coordination, and multilateral cooperation will find this role particularly rewarding. Beyond project coordination, the successful candidate will help facilitate collaboration between governments, international organizations, civil society, and legal experts while supporting one of the most ambitious international efforts to advance the Rights of Nature within the United Nations framework. The position provides meaningful exposure to global environmental diplomacy, strategic communications, institutional development, and international stakeholder engagement, making it an excellent opportunity for experienced professionals looking to make a lasting impact on international environmental policy. Conclusion The Initiative Coordinator position at forNature represents an outstanding opportunity for experienced professionals passionate about environmental governance, international cooperation, and sustainable development. Working closely with Panama s Ministry of Environment and a broad network of international stakeholders, the successful candidate will coordinate high-level legal, diplomatic, operational, and communications activities supporting the advancement of the United Nations Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature.With competitive compensation, international exposure, meaningful responsibilities, and the chance to contribute to a transformative global environmental initiative, this role is ideal for professionals who thrive in fast-paced, multicultural environments and are committed to advancing environmental justice and global cooperation. title: National Geographic Society & The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026: Fully Remote 8-Week Global Opportunity with $500 Stipend for Young Conservation Leaders
summary: Applications are now open for the National Geographic Society The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026, an exciting international opportunity designed for young people who are passionate about environmental conservation, geography, mapping, and data-driven storytelling. This fully remote, part-time externship provides participants with the opportunity to work alongside experts from two of the world s leading conservation organizations the National Geographic Society and The Nature Conservancy while developing practical skills in Geographic Information Systems (GIS), community conservation, data visualization, environmental research, and science communication. Running for eight weeks , the externship offers a flexible schedule requiring approximately 10 hours per week , making it suitable for students and young professionals who want to gain valuable international experience while balancing their studies or other commitments. Participants who successfully complete the program will also receive a $500 educational stipend to help offset internet and technology costs associated with participation. About the National Geographic Society The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation Externship Environmental challenges such as biodiversity loss, climate change, freshwater scarcity, and marine ecosystem degradation continue to affect communities across the globe. Solving these challenges requires innovative thinkers who can use science, technology, data, and storytelling to create meaningful change. The National Geographic Society and The Nature Conservancy have partnered to launch this unique externship to equip young people with practical conservation skills while empowering them to address environmental challenges within their own communities. Participants will learn how geographic information and mapping technologies can be used to understand conservation issues, communicate scientific findings, and influence local action. Rather than focusing only on theory, the program combines learning with practical application, allowing participants to complete hands-on projects using real-world environmental data. Externship Overview The program offers an engaging learning experience with the following features: Duration: 8 weeks Start Date: 14 September 2026 Format: Fully remote Commitment: Approximately 10 hours per week Educational Stipend: $500 upon successful completion Meetings: Recorded for flexible participation Eligibility Age: 18–25 years Geographic Eligibility: Open worldwide Because the externship is conducted entirely online, participants from any country can take part without relocating. What Participants Will Learn Throughout the eight-week program, participants will explore major conservation issues while developing technical and professional skills that are highly valued across environmental and sustainability careers. Major learning areas include: 1. Biodiversity and Community Conservation Participants will study some of today s most pressing environmental issues, including: Biodiversity loss Conservation solutions Marine ecosystem protection Freshwater conservation Community-based conservation initiatives They will also examine the relationship between geography, ecosystems, and local communities. 2. Geographic Information Systems (GIS) One of the major highlights of the externship is practical training in Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Participants will gain foundational knowledge of GIS technologies used worldwide to: Collect geographic information Manage environmental datasets Analyze spatial information Create professional maps Support conservation planning Visualize environmental challenges The program uses Esri GIS mapping tools , one of the world s leading geographic information platforms. 3. Data Visualization Participants will learn how to transform complex environmental information into visual stories that communicate conservation challenges effectively. This includes: Visual mapping Spatial data presentation Interactive storytelling Geographic data interpretation 4. Community Research Participants will conduct research focused on conservation issues affecting their own local communities. This includes: Identifying environmental challenges Collecting location-based information Researching local biodiversity concerns Investigating community conservation efforts 5. Public Speaking and Science Communication Strong communication is essential for conservation leadership. Participants will build confidence by learning how to: Present research findings Explain complex scientific concepts Deliver engaging presentations Communicate conservation solutions effectively 6. Conservation Storytelling Using Esri StoryMaps, participants will create engaging digital stories that combine: Maps Images Research Geographic information Environmental narratives These projects become valuable portfolio pieces for future academic and professional opportunities. Projects Participants Will Complete Throughout the externship, participants will work on practical assignments, including: Researching conservation issues in their communities Creating maps using GIS software Visualizing environmental data Developing interactive Esri StoryMaps Presenting conservation solutions Collaborating with conservation experts Skills Participants Will Gain By the end of the externship, participants will have developed a broad range of transferable skills, including: Conservation Literacy Participants will gain a deeper understanding of: Biodiversity conservation Environmental sustainability Geographic conservation strategies Community resilience Research Skills Participants will practice: Primary research Secondary research Data collection Information analysis Insight development Community-Based Problem Solving Participants will learn structured approaches for: Identifying conservation gaps Designing realistic environmental solutions Addressing local conservation challenges Cross-Sector Collaboration Participants will work with professionals from: National Geographic Society The Nature Conservancy They will gain valuable exposure to collaborative conservation work involving scientists, communicators, and community organizations. Portfolio Development Every participant will produce a professional Esri StoryMap that demonstrates their: Research ability Mapping skills Data visualization expertise Conservation storytelling This project can strengthen future applications for scholarships, fellowships, internships, employment, and grants. Systems Thinking Participants will explore how global environmental challenges affect local ecosystems and communities while developing solutions that connect local action with broader conservation goals. What Participants Receive Successful participants will benefit from numerous professional development opportunities, including: Hands-on conservation experience Direct mentorship from National Geographic Society experts Guidance from The Nature Conservancy professionals GIS and mapping training Environmental research experience Science communication skills Public speaking experience Portfolio-ready conservation project International networking opportunities Flexible online participation $500 educational stipend upon successful completion About the National Geographic Society Founded in 1888 , the National Geographic Society is a global nonprofit organization committed to advancing science, exploration, education, and storytelling. The organization has: Awarded more than 15,000 grants worldwide Supported research across all seven continents Reached millions of students through educational initiatives Inspired global audiences through science and exploration About The Nature Conservancy The Nature Conservancy is one of the world s leading environmental nonprofit organizations. Its mission focuses on protecting the lands and waters upon which all life depends while addressing: Climate change Biodiversity conservation Sustainable ecosystems Community resilience The organization works globally to create a future where both people and nature thrive. Why You Should Apply This externship is ideal for young people interested in: Environmental conservation Climate action Geography GIS mapping Sustainability Environmental communication Research Science storytelling Data visualization Community engagement APPLY HERE No previous experience in GIS, conservation, or environmental science is required. Participants only need curiosity, enthusiasm, and a willingness to learn. Who Should Apply? The externship is especially suitable for individuals who: Are between 18 and 25 years old Care about environmental issues Want to understand how conservation affects communities Are interested in GIS and mapping technologies Enjoy research and problem-solving Want to build an international professional portfolio Prefer flexible remote learning opportunities Have not previously participated in a National Geographic Society + The Nature Conservancy Externship Application Process Interested applicants should submit their applications through the official application platform before the closing date. Because applications are expected to be highly competitive, prospective participants are encouraged to apply as early as possible. Important Dates Application Deadline: 30 August 2026 Externship Start Date: 14 September 2026 Duration: 8 weeks Commitment: Approximately 10 hours per week Mode: Fully remote Visit HERE to learn more about the National Geographic Society The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026 Conclusion The National Geographic Society The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026 offers an outstanding opportunity for young people worldwide to gain practical conservation experience while learning from internationally recognized environmental organizations. Through expert mentorship, GIS training, conservation research, and storytelling, participants will develop skills that are increasingly valuable in careers related to sustainability, environmental policy, conservation science, education, and community development. Beyond the technical knowledge, participants will build a professional portfolio, expand their global network, and contribute meaningful conservation solutions within their own communities. With a fully remote format, flexible schedule, and a $500 educational stipend, this externship provides an accessible pathway for the next generation of conservation leaders to make a lasting impact. For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org . title: NEH Collaborative Research Grants 2026 in the USA | Up to $250,000 for Humanities Research Projects
summary: The National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) is inviting applications for its Collaborative Research Grants 2026, a prestigious funding opportunity designed to advance knowledge in the humanities through collaborative scholarship. The program supports teams of researchers working together on projects that produce significant interpretive outputs such as books, digital publications, scholarly websites, peer-reviewed journal issues, and other sustainable research resources. With awards of up to $250,000 , this funding opportunity provides scholars and institutions with the resources needed to pursue innovative humanities research that contributes to a deeper understanding of the history and culture of the United States and Western civilization. About the NEH Collaborative Research Program The Collaborative Research Program supports teams of scholars engaged in humanities research that addresses important research questions through collaborative approaches. Projects may be based within a single discipline or bring together expertise from multiple fields. NEH encourages projects that: * Advance humanities scholarship. * Incorporate diverse perspectives and approaches. * Explore new areas of inquiry. * Foster interdisciplinary collaboration. * Produce tangible and sustainable scholarly outputs. Collaborators may come from a single institution or multiple institutions, and international partnerships are welcome provided that scholars at U.S. institutions make substantial contributions to the project. Funding Categories The 2026 competition supports three project categories: 1. Planning International Collaboration Supports the development of international humanities research partnerships and collaborative projects. Maximum Award: Up to $50,000 2. Manuscript Preparation Supports collaborative research leading to scholarly books, edited volumes, and peer-reviewed publications. 3. Scholarly Digital Project Supports the creation of digital humanities resources, databases, websites, and digital publications that advance humanities scholarship. Funding Benefits Successful applicants may receive: * Funding of up to $250,000 depending on project category. * Support for collaborative humanities research. * Resources for manuscript development and publication. * Funding for digital humanities projects. * Opportunities to establish international research partnerships. * Support for interdisciplinary and cross-institutional collaboration. Expected Project Outputs Projects must result in a tangible and sustainable product, including: * Co-authored books * Edited scholarly volumes * Themed issues of peer-reviewed journals * Digital publications * Scholarly websites * Digital humanities resources Outputs should demonstrate meaningful collaboration and contribute to significant humanities research questions. Eligible Applicants The program is open to organizations and institutions supporting humanities research teams. Collaborators may come from: * Universities and colleges * Research institutions * Cultural organizations * Humanities centers * Nonprofit organizations International collaboration is encouraged, but U.S.-based scholars must play a significant role in the project. 2026 Program Priority For the 2026 funding cycle, proposed projects must focus on: * The history of the United States * The culture of the United States * Western civilization Applicants should ensure that their projects align clearly with these thematic priorities. Project Duration Depending on the funding category, projects may receive support for up to: Three Years This allows research teams sufficient time to complete substantial humanities projects and produce high-quality scholarly outputs. Application Timeline | Application Opens | July 7, 2026 | | Application Deadline | September 16, 2026 | Applicants are encouraged to begin preparations early to allow sufficient time for institutional approvals and registration requirements. Application Process Step 1: Review the Funding Opportunity Carefully read the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and related application guidance documents. Step 2: Complete Required Registrations Applicants must have active registrations with: * SAM.gov * Grants.gov Organizations should verify that their registrations are current before beginning the application process. Step 3: Prepare the Application Develop a strong proposal that clearly outlines: * Research objectives * Collaborative structure * Project methodology * Expected outcomes * Dissemination plans Step 4: Submit Through Grants.gov Applications must be submitted electronically through Grants.gov before the deadline. Why Apply? The NEH Collaborative Research Grants represent one of the leading funding opportunities for humanities scholars seeking to undertake ambitious collaborative research projects. Whether developing a major scholarly publication, creating innovative digital resources, or building international partnerships, this program provides the financial support needed to generate lasting contributions to humanities scholarship. The program also encourages interdisciplinary collaboration and supports projects that bring together diverse expertise to address complex research questions in new and meaningful ways. Contact Information Division of Research National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) 📧 [collaborative@neh.gov](mailto:collaborative@neh.gov) 📞 202-606-8200 Conclusion The NEH Collaborative Research Grants 2026 offer a remarkable opportunity for humanities researchers and institutions to collaborate on projects that expand knowledge, generate impactful scholarship, and contribute to a deeper understanding of the United States and Western civilization. With funding of up to $250,000, support for international collaboration, and opportunities to create lasting scholarly resources, this program is ideal for teams seeking to advance innovative humanities research. Interested applicants should begin preparing their proposals now and submit their applications before the September 16, 2026 deadline. Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage . title: Communications Officer (Digital & Multimedia) at UNICEF Fiji: Complete Guide to the 2026 National UN Volunteer Opportunity in Suva
summary: The United Nations Children s Fund (UNICEF), through the United Nations Volunteers (UNV) programme, is inviting qualified professionals to apply for the Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) National UN Volunteer assignment based in Suva, Fiji . This is an excellent opportunity for experienced communications professionals with strong digital media, storytelling, multimedia production, and social media management skills to contribute to improving the lives of children and young people across the Pacific region. The assignment offers professionals an opportunity to work directly with UNICEF s Communication Section, supporting advocacy campaigns, multimedia storytelling, digital communications, donor visibility initiatives, and audience engagement across 14 Pacific Island countries. If you have experience in digital communications, content creation, photography, videography, multimedia editing, analytics, and strategic communication, this assignment provides a meaningful platform to apply your expertise while supporting one of the world s leading humanitarian organizations. About UNICEF UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to protect the rights and wellbeing of every child. Its mission is to ensure that every child survives, thrives, learns, and is protected from violence, discrimination, and exploitation. Within the Pacific region, UNICEF serves: Cook Islands Fiji Kiribati Marshall Islands Federated States of Micronesia Nauru Niue Palau Samoa Solomon Islands Tokelau Tonga Tuvalu Vanuatu Together, these countries are home to approximately 2.3 million people , including 1.2 million children and youth , living across more than 660 islands and atolls spread over approximately 17.2 million square kilometres of the Pacific Ocean. Several countries within the region—including Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tuvalu—are classified as Fragile States under World Bank/OECD criteria, making UNICEF s work particularly significant. About the Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) Assignment The Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) will be part of UNICEF Pacific s Communications Section and will report directly to the Digital Communication Officer . The Communications Section supports all UNICEF programme areas through strategic communication, advocacy, media engagement, branding, digital outreach, and social media campaigns. The team also leads advocacy around four major regional priorities: Violence against children Climate action Water security Nutrition The selected volunteer will help strengthen UNICEF s digital presence, produce engaging multimedia content, enhance donor visibility, support youth participation, and amplify UNICEF s advocacy messages through innovative storytelling. Assignment Information Item Details Host Organization UNICEF Volunteer Programme United Nations Volunteers (UNV) Position Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) Duty Station Suva, Fiji Assignment Type National UN Volunteer Volunteer Category Specialist Work Arrangement Full-time Work Location On UN Premises Duration 12 Months Extension Possibility Yes Expected Start Date 24 August 2026 Number of Vacancies 1 Main Responsibilities The Communications Officer will undertake a wide range of responsibilities covering digital communications, multimedia production, analytics, storytelling, advocacy, and volunteer engagement. 1. Digital Communication Planning and Publishing The successful candidate will support UNICEF s online communication strategy by: Planning digital communication activities. Producing digital communication materials. Publishing content across UNICEF s website and digital platforms. Supporting social media campaigns. Coordinating promotional campaigns. Developing communication materials aligned with regional and global priorities. Supporting donor visibility planning. Coordinating production timelines. Monitoring donor branding requirements. Maintaining influencer and advocacy databases. Supporting youth engagement initiatives. Assisting online participation campaigns. 2. Multimedia Storytelling A major component of the role involves creating compelling multimedia stories that demonstrate UNICEF s impact. Responsibilities include: Producing social media reels. Editing short videos. Creating photo stories. Designing graphics. Preparing presentation assets. Using existing photo and video libraries. Capturing photographs during events. Recording field missions. Covering programme visits. Documenting humanitarian activities. Working with programme teams to identify impactful stories. Simplifying complex development programmes into engaging public stories. Coordinating interviews. Supporting scripting. Managing filming schedules. Editing content. Incorporating feedback. Preparing final products for publication. 3. Ensuring UNICEF Brand Standards The officer will ensure all communication materials comply with UNICEF standards by following: UNICEF branding guidelines. Ethical storytelling practices. Child safeguarding policies. Image consent procedures. Accessibility standards. Inclusion principles. 4. Digital Analytics and Performance Monitoring The role also requires continuous monitoring of digital performance. Responsibilities include: Tracking engagement rates. Monitoring audience growth. Measuring reach. Assessing impressions. Reviewing click-through rates. Preparing campaign performance reports. Identifying successful content trends. Testing new communication approaches. Monitoring audience feedback. Detecting misinformation. Reporting reputational risks. Supporting positive digital engagement. 5. Supporting the UN Volunteers Programme As part of the assignment, the volunteer will also: Promote volunteerism. Participate in UN Volunteer activities. Celebrate International Volunteer Day. Produce annual volunteer reports. Share field stories for UNV publications. Mentor newly arrived volunteers through the Buddy Programme. Encourage organizations to utilize UN Online Volunteering services. Required Skills and Experience Applicants should possess at least three years of professional experience in communications or related fields. Essential competencies include: Professional digital communications experience. Social media management. Multimedia editing. Photography. Videography. Storytelling. Graphic content production. Copywriting. Editing. Proofreading. Project management. Organizational skills. Communication planning. Digital monitoring. Analytics. Teamwork. Remote collaboration. Strong interpersonal communication. Candidates should also demonstrate commitment to UNICEF s CRITAS values: Care Respect Integrity Trust Accountability Sustainability Desirable Skills Applicants with the following additional skills will have an advantage: Digital analytics experience. Canva. Adobe Premiere Pro. Adobe Photoshop. Adobe Lightroom. Adobe Illustrator. Adobe InDesign. Content Management Systems (CMS). NGO experience. UN experience. Spreadsheet management. Database management. Technical writing. Translating technical documents into public-friendly messages. Educational Requirements Applicants must possess: A Bachelor s degree in: Communications Journalism Or another closely related discipline Language Requirements Applicants must demonstrate: Fluent English (required) Core Competencies UNICEF seeks professionals who demonstrate: Accountability Adaptability Flexibility Building Trust Commitment Motivation Continuous Learning Communication Creativity Ethics Integrity Planning Organizing Professionalism Respect for Diversity Self-management Technological Awareness Teamwork Areas of Expertise Successful candidates should have experience in one or more of the following: Communications Public Information Advocacy Writing Editing Proofreading Research Reporting Knowledge Management Eligibility Criteria Applicants must: Be between 18 and 80 years of age. Be a national of Fiji , a legal resident of Fiji, or hold refugee status in Fiji. Have at least three years of relevant professional experience . Meet the required educational qualifications. Demonstrate fluency in English. Living and Working in Fiji The assignment is based in Suva , the capital city of Fiji. UNICEF notes that: Fiji is considered a middle-income country. Basic services are readily available. The country is widely recognized for its welcoming and friendly communities. Volunteers are expected to arrange their own accommodation and living arrangements. Standard personal security precautions should be observed. Inclusivity and Equal Opportunity UNICEF and the United Nations Volunteers programme strongly encourage diversity and inclusion. Applications are welcomed regardless of: Gender Race Religion Nationality Ethnicity Disability Sexual orientation Gender identity Language Social origin Pregnancy Age Reasonable accommodation is available for volunteers with disabilities throughout recruitment and during the assignment. COVID-19 Requirement Selected volunteers must generally provide proof of full COVID-19 vaccination with a World Health Organization (WHO)-endorsed vaccine before assuming duty, where applicable under UNICEF policies. Certain remote assignments or assignments without community interaction may be exempt according to UNICEF guidelines. Scam Warning Applicants should remember that: The United Nations never charges application fees. No payment is required at any stage of recruitment. Applicants should be cautious of fraudulent recruitment schemes and only apply through official UN platforms. Why You Should Apply This assignment offers communications professionals an exceptional opportunity to: Build experience within UNICEF. Strengthen digital communication and multimedia production skills. Work on high-impact advocacy campaigns. Produce stories that improve children s lives. Gain exposure to international development communication. Collaborate with experienced communication professionals. Support youth engagement across the Pacific. Develop expertise in donor visibility and digital analytics. Contribute directly to UNICEF s mission of protecting children s rights. APPLY HERE Application Deadline No application deadline has been specified in the vacancy information. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible, as recruitment may close once a suitable number of applications has been received. Visit HERE to learn more about the Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) at UNICEF Fiji. Conclusion The UNICEF Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) National UN Volunteer assignment presents an outstanding opportunity for experienced communications professionals in Fiji who are passionate about digital storytelling, multimedia production, and advocacy. Working within UNICEF s Pacific Office, the selected volunteer will play a central role in creating compelling digital content that highlights the organization s impact across 14 Pacific Island countries while strengthening public awareness of children s rights and development priorities. Beyond professional growth, this assignment provides the chance to contribute to meaningful humanitarian work, collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, and support campaigns that influence policy, engage young people, and improve the lives of children throughout the Pacific region. Qualified candidates who meet the eligibility requirements are encouraged to submit their applications promptly through the official United Nations Volunteers recruitment platform. title: Oppenheimer Memorial Trust Postgraduate Scholarships 2027 in South Africa: Fully Supported Master’s, Doctoral and Postdoctoral Funding for Outstanding Researchers
summary: The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust (OMT) has officially opened applications for its prestigious Postgraduate Scholarships for students planning to begin their studies between January and June 2027 . The Trust continues its long-standing commitment to developing exceptional academic talent by supporting outstanding scholars pursuing Master s, Doctoral, and Postdoctoral studies in South Africa and, in exceptional cases, internationally. The scholarship is designed for individuals with an exceptional academic record who aspire to make significant contributions to academia, scientific research, innovation, development, public policy, and other fields that advance knowledge and benefit society. Every year, the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust awards a limited number of highly competitive scholarships to scholars who demonstrate excellence, leadership potential, and a commitment to using their advanced education to contribute meaningfully to South Africa s future. Applications for students intending to commence studies between January and June 2027 are currently open and will close on 31 August 2026 . About the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust is one of South Africa s leading philanthropic organizations dedicated to supporting higher education, research, youth development, and initiatives that strengthen the country s knowledge economy. Through its postgraduate scholarship programme, the Trust invests in future academics, researchers, innovators, and professionals whose work has the potential to address national and global challenges. The scholarship programme has supported numerous distinguished researchers and scholars whose work has gained international recognition across multiple disciplines. The Trust believes that investing in highly talented individuals contributes directly to strengthening South Africa s research capacity, universities, innovation ecosystem, and long-term development. OMT Postgraduate Scholarship Programme 2027 The scholarship programme supports postgraduate studies at three academic levels: Master s Degree Doctoral (PhD) Degree Postdoctoral Research Each year, only a limited number of scholarships are awarded, making the programme highly competitive. Successful applicants are expected to demonstrate exceptional academic achievement together with clear plans for using their education to contribute to research, teaching, development, or other knowledge-driven sectors. International Study Opportunities The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust also provides funding for international postgraduate study , although this opportunity is reserved only for exceptional candidates. Applicants seeking international scholarships must demonstrate one or more of the following: Their proposed programme is in a unique or highly specialized discipline that is not readily available in South Africa. The intended international institution offers expertise unavailable locally. Study under internationally recognized experts or global leaders will significantly advance their field. International training will contribute meaningfully to their future academic or research career and ultimately benefit South Africa. International scholarships are therefore considered only in exceptional circumstances and require strong academic justification. Fields of Study Applications are welcomed from all academic disciplines , ensuring that scholars from diverse areas of study have an opportunity to compete for funding. However, the Trust specifically excludes: Master of Business Administration (MBA) programmes Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) programmes Programmes with a narrow commercial focus Apart from these exclusions, applicants across sciences, engineering, humanities, social sciences, medicine, agriculture, environmental sciences, education, arts, technology, law, and many other disciplines are encouraged to apply. Who Should Apply? The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust seeks applicants who demonstrate exceptional academic ability together with a strong vision for their future contribution to society. Ideal candidates include individuals who: Have consistently demonstrated academic excellence. Intend to pursue careers in: Academia Research Innovation Development Public policy Related knowledge-intensive sectors. Have well-developed postgraduate research plans. Show the potential to become leaders in their disciplines. Intend to use their expertise to strengthen research and development within South Africa. Preference for Local Universities Although international study is supported in exceptional cases, the Trust indicates that preference may be given to students pursuing postgraduate studies at South African universities. This reflects the Trust s commitment to strengthening local higher education institutions while still supporting international opportunities where clearly justified. Scholarship Features Successful scholars benefit from: Funding for Master s studies. Funding for Doctoral (PhD) studies. Funding for Postdoctoral research. Possible international scholarship support for exceptional candidates. Recognition through one of South Africa s most prestigious postgraduate scholarship programmes. Opportunities to advance academic and research careers. Support for research that contributes to South Africa s development. Access to a respected network of scholars and researchers. Selection Process The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust follows a highly competitive selection process. Applications are assessed based on: Academic excellence. Quality of the proposed study or research. title: Bayreuth Humboldt Centre Research Grants 2026–2027 ; Starter and Short Term Funding Opportunities
summary: Introduction The University of Bayreuth Centre of International Excellence “Alexander von Humboldt” (Bayreuth Humboldt Centre) has established itself as a hub for fostering international academic collaboration, advancing interdisciplinary research, and strengthening global scholarly networks. Through its Starter Grant Programme (2027) and Short Term Grant Programme (2026) , the Centre provides researchers from around the world with opportunities to engage in innovative projects, collaborate with local hosts at Bayreuth, and contribute to the university’s vibrant research ecosystem. These grants are not merely financial awards; they are instruments of academic exchange designed to break down barriers between disciplines, cultures, and generations of researchers. The Centre’s mission is to support projects of top academic quality, encourage diversity, and promote gender equality in research. By offering structured funding opportunities, the Bayreuth Humboldt Centre ensures that scholars can pursue ambitious projects while benefiting from the university’s infrastructure, networks, and intellectual environment. The Starter Grant Programme provides €10,000 to support project costs, with an additional monthly family allowance for grantees accompanied by children. Successful completion of a Starter Grant opens the door to a Booster Grant (€20,000), contingent on documented outcomes such as joint publications, workshops, or conferences. The Short Term Grant Programme supports research stays of 1–3 weeks, reimbursing travel and accommodation expenses up to €3,500. This programme is ideal for scholars seeking to establish collaborations, initiate joint projects, or explore new research directions in a condensed timeframe. Both programmes require applicants to identify a local host at Bayreuth prior to submission, ensuring that projects are grounded in meaningful collaboration. The grants are open to all disciplines, with specific rulings for African Studies due to German Research Foundation regulations. By participating in these programmes, researchers gain not only financial support but also access to Bayreuth’s world-class research networks, facilities, and intellectual community. The application deadline for both programmes is September 15, 2026 . Programme Details 1. Programme Overview Starter Grant Programme (2027): €10,000 award, family allowance, eligibility for Booster Grant (€20,000). Short Term Grant Programme (2026): Up to €3,500 reimbursement for travel and accommodation, 1–3 week stays. Both programmes emphasise collaboration with a local host at Bayreuth . 2. Programme Goals Promote academic exchange across disciplines and cultures. Strengthen international networking with leading universities worldwide. Encourage interdisciplinary research addressing societal challenges. Support diversity and gender equality in research. 3. Candidate Requirements Completed PhD (including diploma). Affiliation with institutions abroad. Projects must demonstrate academic excellence and potential for networking. Applications must adhere to Application Guidelines . 4. Experience Bayreuth – Collaboration with Local Host Applicants must identify a local host prior to submission. Hosts provide office/lab space and infrastructure. Projects must benefit both the candidate and the host. 5. Funding Details Starter Grant: €10,000 + €250/month family allowance. Booster Grant: €20,000 follow‑up funding upon successful completion. Short Term Grant: Up to €3,500 reimbursement for travel/accommodation. 6. Application Process Submit complete application via online form. Required documents: personal statement, CV, project details. Deadline: September 15, 2026 . Selection is merit‑based, focusing on academic excellence and project quality. Apply HERE today! Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q1: What is the purpose of the Bayreuth Humboldt Centre Grants? The grants aim to foster international collaboration, support interdisciplinary research, and strengthen Bayreuth’s global academic networks. They provide financial support and institutional affiliation to researchers pursuing innovative projects. Q2: Who can apply for these grants? Academics, independent scholars, and professionals affiliated with institutions abroad who have completed their PhD are eligible. Applicants must propose projects of high academic quality and identify a local host at Bayreuth. Q3: What is the difference between the Starter Grant and the Short Term Grant? The Starter Grant (€10,000) supports longer-term projects and includes eligibility for a follow-up Booster Grant (€20,000). The Short Term Grant (up to €3,500) supports research stays of 1–3 weeks, covering travel and accommodation expenses. Q4: Are the grants open to all disciplines? Yes, both grants are open to all disciplines. However, specific rulings apply to African Studies hosts due to German Research Foundation regulations. Q5: What are the key selection criteria? Selection is merit-based, focusing on the academic excellence of the applicant and the cooperative project, as evidenced by publications, project design, and potential for networking. Q6: What support do grantees receive beyond funding? Grantees gain institutional affiliation, access to Bayreuth’s library and research facilities, office and lab space, and integration into the university’s research networks. Q7: What is expected of grantees during their fellowship? Grantees must collaborate with their local host, utilise Bayreuth’s infrastructure, and submit a report documenting outcomes within 15 months of acceptance. Q8: Can applicants with families apply? Yes. Starter Grant recipients accompanied by children receive an additional monthly family allowance of €250. Q9: What is the application process? Applicants must submit a complete application via the online form, including required documents, by September 15, 2026 . Q10: What happens after completing a Starter Grant? Successful grantees may apply for a Booster Grant (€20,000), contingent on documented outcomes such as publications or conferences. Q11: How does the programme promote diversity? The Centre views diversity as an asset and actively encourages applications from female scholars and individuals who can enhance the university’s research profile. Q12: What are the reporting requirements? A report must be submitted 15 months after acceptance, documenting project outcomes and contributions. Visit HERE to learn more about the Bayreuth Humboldt Centre Research Grants 2026–2027 Conclusion The University of Bayreuth Centre of International Excellence “Alexander von Humboldt” Grants 2026–2027 represent a significant opportunity for researchers worldwide to engage in high-quality projects, foster international collaboration, and contribute to Bayreuth’s dynamic academic environment. The Starter Grant Programme provides substantial funding for ambitious projects, with the potential for follow-up support through the Booster Grant. The Short Term Grant Programme offers targeted support for shorter research stays, enabling scholars to initiate collaborations and explore new directions. Both programmes emphasise collaboration with local hosts, integration into Bayreuth’s research networks, and adherence to rigorous academic standards. By participating, grantees gain not only financial support but also institutional affiliation, access to resources, and the chance to contribute to a diverse and inclusive research community. With an application deadline of September 15, 2026 , these grants are a gateway to innovation, networking, and scholarly impact. For researchers seeking to expand their horizons and engage with one of Germany’s leading universities, the Bayreuth Humboldt Centre Grants offer a transformative opportunity. To explore and lean more about other grant opportunities, visit the OFY page HERE . title: Skoll Scholarship 2027 at the University of Oxford: Fully Funded Oxford MBA Scholarship for Social Entrepreneurs Driving Systemic Change

The Skoll Scholarship is a prestigious scholarship that enables social entrepreneurs to pursue an Oxford MBA with full tuition funding, partial living expenses, and access to the Skoll Scholar community. What expenses does the scholarship cover? The scholarship covers: Full Oxford MBA course fees. Partial living expenses. Who is the scholarship intended for? It is designed for social entrepreneurs committed to creating and leading ventures that address significant social and environmental challenges. How do I apply? Applicants must first apply to the Oxford MBA at Saïd Business School and submit responses to the Skoll Scholarship essay questions as part of their MBA application. What happens after submitting my MBA application? The MBA Admissions Team evaluates your application for admission. If admitted, your application automatically proceeds to the Skoll Scholarship Selection Committee. What is the scholarship selection process? The process includes: MBA admission review. Scholarship review. Shortlisting. Completion of a Logistics and Reference Form. First-stage online interview. Final online interview. Does the scholarship value diversity? Yes. The programme encourages applications from women, historically underrepresented groups, and individuals from the Global South while promoting an inclusive and collaborative community. Why You Should Apply The Skoll Scholarship is more than financial assistance—it is an investment in visionary leaders committed to solving some of the world s most urgent social and environmental challenges. By combining the Oxford MBA with financial support and membership in a global community of social innovators, the scholarship equips participants with the knowledge, leadership skills, and international networks needed to expand the reach and effectiveness of their work. For entrepreneurs who are already creating impact and aspire to drive systemic change, the Skoll Scholarship offers an unparalleled opportunity to learn, collaborate, and accelerate positive transformation. If you are leading a social enterprise, tackling complex societal challenges, and ready to enhance your leadership through one of the world s leading business schools, consider preparing a strong Oxford MBA application and applying for the Skoll Scholarship during one of the eligible admissions stages.
